 The Booming Business of Beauty on TikTok Shop
 The latest findings in Circana’s special beauty report look at how brands on TikTok Shop continue to drive the category’s overall growth and brand discovery globally.

 Since TikTok Shop launched in the U.S. in 2023, it has quickly become a major hub for beauty .
 Thus far, the platform’s beauty and personal care category has seen $2.08 billion in sales — which makes it the largest category on the social media platform’s e-commerce arm, outperforming women’s apparel by more than $500 million, according to Circana’s latest beauty report’s data from January to June 2026.
 TikTok Shop has also become a beauty-first commerce platform across various markets, not just seeing strength in the U.S. Beauty ranks number two in the U.K., which reinforces its role within the social commerce space.

 As a whole, TikTok is its own beauty retailer. In comparison to other e-commerce beauty retailers, TikTok Shop ranks third in beauty e-commerce — trailing behind pure-play e-commerce and specialty retailer channels. And within the overall beauty retail space, TikTok’s beauty ranks below off-price beauty retailers.

 TikTok has also become one of the major ways for consumer discovery and purchasing. The overall shopping ecosystem of the social media app remains discovery-driven and democratized.
 Leading categories are sold by hundreds or thousands of individual shops, which allows for emerging brands to compete with established players on the global stage. Consumers have become more responsive to discovery — and less loyal than traditional retail shoppers. TikTok has created a significant opportunity for challenger brands to grow.
 Data from January to June 2026. 
 “The platform has created a more democratized beauty marketplace where authenticity and results matter more than legacy status,” Larissa Jensen, senior vice president and global industry adviser of Circana, told Fairchild Studio . “Consumers are rewarding brands that can quickly demonstrate value and build trust through creators.”
 Demographically, TikTok has always maintained a reputation of being most popular among Gen Z audiences, but that’s not always the case; social commerce spending actually skews higher toward Gen X and older Millennial audiences. Hispanic and African American households also collectively drive more than a third (36 percent) of TikTok Shop’s beauty spending — which highlights the importance of diverse products and paying attention to a range of multicultural audiences.
 Consumers on the platform also continue to be highly engaged with the beauty industry. On average, shoppers spent $24.39 per unit, only $6 below the $31 price point for cross-industry spending.
 Notably, there is a vast and diverse mix within the brands consumers are gravitating toward — whether it’s K-beauty skin and hair care, Middle Eastern-driven fragrance brands, traditional prestige alongside small, independent brands.
 Shoppers are continuously on the hunt for brands that are authentic and niche — as opposed to purchasing traditional prestige category leaders, as TikTok consumers are more influenced by creator credibility and efficacy rather than heritage brand awareness. Now they are turning to brands like Medicube, Based, Bask & Lather, Bare Anatomy and Root Labs.
 “Today’s beauty consumer is highly informed and increasingly global in their purchasing behavior,” continued Jensen. “Platforms like TikTok are accelerating awareness and trial of brands that may have had limited exposure through conventional retail channels.”
 Data from January to June 2026. 
 Within beauty, the biggest segments seeing traction include fragrance ($218 million for unisex, men’s and women’s combined), skin care ($161 million), moisturizers and mists ($82 million) and serums and essences ($78 million).
 Today’s shoppers are also increasingly spending their money on complete regimens, bundles and sets that have proven results. Consumers are most responding to product claims with messaging around collagen, glass skin, firming, glow and visible transformations.
 And within this result-driven skin care segment, the top-selling products on TikTok are Medicube’s PDRN eye patches, Medicube glass glow sets, Dr.Melaxin collagen sets and Medicube’s PDRN collagen products.
 Most noteworthy is that all these products fall under the K-beauty category — which continues to drive and shape the landscape of consumer behavior. From January to June 2026, top brands Medicube, Dr.Melaxin, Jiyu, Sungboon, CosRx, Skin1004 and Anua has collectively generated more than $245 million in sales.
 Circana’s report authors noted that these numbers indicate that TikTok consumers are actively seeking out K-beauty brands and trust the platform for discovery of emerging global beauty products.
 “The strongest-performing categories on TikTok share a common theme: They combine education, inspiration and proof of performance. Consumers are responding to products that fit seamlessly into routines and offer visible benefits,” explained Jensen.
 Data from January to June 2026. 
 Another category that has seen notable consumer interest is hair health. Across the broader market, shoppers are gravitating toward products that address hair growth, scalp health, hair density, curl care, repair and strengthening solutions.
 The fastest-growing and largest hair care brands among TikTok sellers are Based Bodyworks, Bask & Lather, Color Wow, Dr. Groot, Bare Anatomy and Root Labs — seeing more than $85 million in sales.
 And despite a limited sensory experience within the app, fragrance continues to be a growth leader with consumers relying on blind buys via storytelling, reviews and creator recommendations. Lattafa, Bellavita, Dossier and Armaf are some of the biggest brands on the TikTok marketplace, with more than $53 million in sales.
 Within accessories, tools and devices, the highest-revenue categories are curlers and straighteners, massage devices, skin care devices, hair dryers, and hair trimmers — accounting for $158 million of the market. Circana said this heavy investment by shoppers into beauty tool purchases continues to demonstrate consumers’ willingness to invest in routines and experiences.
 “The pace of brand disruption on TikTok is remarkable. Products can move from niche discovery to meaningful sales volume in a short period of time when they resonate with consumers and creators alike,” concluded Jensen.
